scope: Public primary-source documentation and code only. No paid model calls, benchmark execution, or local held-out records were accessed for this research.
interpretation_boundary: A verified author statement is not an independently reproduced score. Repeated development-set success does not establish unseen-set generalization.

findings.status: The project itself acknowledges targeted known-failure fixes and a retrieval-versus-QA comparison error.
verified: The benchmark tracker says the final 99.4-to-100 step added three fixes developed by inspecting three specific failures and calls this teaching to the test.
The tracker says the same questions were used for tuning and measurement, so that result does not demonstrate clean generalization.
The April 14 correction acknowledges that retrieval R@5/R@10 had been compared with competitors' end-to-end QA accuracy and retracts the 100-percent headline.
The correction reports a 96.6-percent raw R@5 reproduction against v3.3.0, and separately claims 98.4-percent R@5 on a 450-question split. These are project claims, not reproductions performed here.
unverified: Independence and correctness of the claimed raw reproduction were not audited here.

The claimed 450-question held-out result was not independently reproduced; the documents also describe inspecting failures on the full benchmark before introducing the split. A later split cannot undo earlier exposure.

version_context.caveat: An old benchmark claim is not evidence that the latest product release has been evaluated.

findings.status: 98.6 percent is a retrieval-only Recall@10 claim, not generated-answer accuracy.
verified: The April 8 report explicitly says no LLM generates an answer. It reports R@5 of 96.4 percent and R@10 of 98.6 percent over 500 questions.
The report uses BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 with a fresh in-memory Qdrant collection for each question. Its benchmark excludes the product's Q-learning component.
The public runner scores recall_any: at least one labeled answer session appears among the top-k sessions. It builds session documents from user turns and does not generate or judge answers.
implications: Finding one gold session does not prove that all multi-session evidence was retrieved or that a reader reasons correctly, updates facts, or abstains.
unverified: No independent reproduction or untouched evaluation split was established by the inspected project sources.
The script accepts longmemeval_s_cleaned.json but the report does not pin the dataset hash, code commit, or an immutable per-question result artifact.

version_context.release_page_displayed: v0.1.0, March 30; page crawl predates this research by five months, so current latest-release status is not established

findings.status: 95.4 percent is the project's task-averaged headline; its reported raw numerator is 466/500, or 93.2 percent per-question accuracy.
verified: The official benchmark page attributes the February 2026 result to a GPT-4.1 reader and bge-small embeddings.
It reports preferences 30/30, multi-session 111/133, knowledge updates 75/78, temporal reasoning 125/133, and combined single-session 125/126.
The author's February 13 account explicitly describes selecting the best prompt per category, then category-specific prompts and a change to task-averaged scoring.
The public repository's benchmark report still leads with an older 76.8-percent result; it does not supply an aligned reproduction of the current headline.

derived_arithmetic.interpretation: The site and post alternate between five and six categories. The exact original six-category breakdown is needed to reconcile the 95.4-percent headline; these arithmetic checks do not prove the headline false.

unverified: No independent frozen-split reproduction was established in the inspected primary sources.

The exact judge snapshot, complete current harness and result provenance, whether dataset question-type labels route the prompts, and any oracle-versus-retrieved context distinction for the final run were not established. Do not infer these from third-party accusations.

version_context.caveat: The release listing does not establish a fresh benchmark of the latest version.

findings.status: The paper's 60.6-percent GPT-4o result is full-history LongMemEval_S QA without Chain-of-Note, not an empty-memory baseline or retrieval recall.
verified: Paper v2, revised March 4, 2025, Figure 3(b) reports GPT-4o at 60.6 percent on approximately 115K-token full histories and 87.0 percent on evidence-only oracle contexts. With Chain-of-Note, those are 64.0 and 92.4 percent.
The official evaluator maps gpt-4o to gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and computes the mean of per-question judgments, with separate per-type reporting.
The repository distinguishes generated-answer evaluation from intermediate retrieval metrics, and says retrieval evaluation skips 30 abstention cases because they lack answer locations.
Using the oracle JSON as an answer-key file for the judge is normal and does not by itself establish that oracle context was supplied to the answer generator.
unverified: No official private train/dev/test split or one-shot scoring rule was found in the inspected README. The user's one-shot held-out constraint is an additional local requirement, not something this research attributes to the official protocol.

local_evaluation_implications: Report end-to-end per-question QA accuracy, retrieval-any recall, retrieval-all evidence support, and task-averaged QA separately, with explicit denominators and abstention handling.
Disclose every development run and human-informed prompt or retrieval change; development-set gains remain development results.

Freeze source, code, model, prompt, selection policy and evaluator before the single authorized held-out evaluation. Never route generation by reference answer, gold evidence, or dataset question type.

Do not select a winning old answer or prompt using gold results, per-case fixes, or repeated held-out retests. Question-only retrieval and citation-guided evidence selection still require an honest untouched-set test of the final fixed policy.
